'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Bob Ehrlich]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Martin O'Malley]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Maryland sidebar}} The '''2006 Maryland gubernatorial election''' was held on November 7, 2006. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Bob Ehrlich]] ran for a second term, but was defeated by the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee, [[List of mayors of Baltimore|Baltimore Mayor]] [[Martin O'Malley]]. Ehrlich was the only incumbent governor to lose a general election in the 2006 midterms. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== *[[Martin O'Malley]], Mayor of [[Baltimore]] ===Campaign=== [[Baltimore]] Mayor [[Martin O'Malley]] and [[Montgomery County, Maryland|Montgomery County]] Executive [[Doug Duncan]] emerged as the two Democratic candidates for governor in late 2005. Early polling indicated that O'Malley would have the advantage in both the Democratic primary and the general election, with a solid lead over Duncan in the primary and a several point lead over Ehrlich in the general.{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2005/oct/24/20051024-103424-5071r/|title=Democrat support plunges for Ehrlich |newspaper=The Washington Times}} As the gubernatorial campaign intensified, Duncan withdrew from the race, citing his diagnosis with clinical depression. In the same announcement, he threw his support behind O'Malley and declined to seek another office in the fall. No other Democratic candidate had announced, so O'Malley was unopposed in the primary election. O'Malley selected [[Anthony Brown (Maryland politician)|Anthony Brown]], a black [[Maryland House of Delegates|State Delegate]] from [[Prince George's County, Maryland|Prince George's County]] and a veteran of the [[Iraq War]], as his running mate. ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results{{Cite web|url=https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2006/results/primary/office_Governor__Lt_Governor.html|title=Official 2006 Gubernatorial Primary Election results for Governor / Lt. Driscoll (P) ===Campaign=== Elected to his first term in [[2002 Maryland gubernatorial election|2002]], incumbent Republican governor [[Bob Ehrlich]] ran for a second term as governor, opposed by the Democratic nominee, [[Martin O'Malley]], the mayor of [[Baltimore]]. Both candidates emerged from uncontested primary elections and a contentious election season began. Early in the campaign, Ehrlich boasted decent approval ratings from [[Maryland]] citizens, with a Gonzalez Research poll taken during October 2005 showing him with a 49% approval rating. and ''The Baltimore Sun'' poll from November 2005 giving the Governor a 50% approval and a 33% disapproval.{{Cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2005/11/06/an-early-edge-for-ehrlichs-rivals/|title=An early edge for Ehrlich's rivals|first=By Andrew A. Green and David|last=Nitkin|website=baltimoresun.com|date=November 6, 2005 }} However, the unpopularity of the national [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] and President [[George W. Bush]] dragged Ehrlich's re-election chances down.{{cite web |author1=Lauren Dezenski |author2=Kevin Robillard |title=Trump makes blue-state Republicans squirm |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2017/02/trump-hogan-baker-blue-states-234452 |website=[[Politico]] |access-date=16 July 2024 |date=1 February 2017}}{{cite news |author1=Matthew Mosk |author2=John Wagner |title=Cardin, O'Malley Win in Statewide Democratic Wave |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2006/11/08/cardin-omalley-win-in-statewide-democratic-wave/745575ba-19e3-4434-8ead-cb2fa86a012d/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=16 July 2024 |date=8 November 2006 |quote=Although both contests remained competitive, the general anti-Republican mood pervading the nation began to weigh on Ehrlich and Steele, who tried to tap national GOP connections for money while trying to avoid an affiliation with Washington as the climate worsened for their party.}} Ehrlich launched attack ads that hit O'Malley on [[crime in Baltimore]] under his tenure as Mayor, calling the murder rate in Baltimore "awful" and "an embarrassment to the state of Maryland."{{Cite news|last=Wagner|first=John|date=2006-09-30|title=Ehrlich Ads Hammer O'Malley on Crime|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|language=en-US|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/09/29/AR2006092901818.html|access-date=2021-07-16|issn=0190-8286}} O'Malley countered with one television ad that featured testimonials from local community leaders, [[Howard County, Maryland|Howard County]] Executive [[James N.
